competitive_landscape: Launches from the Bodeguita docks and private boats serve the Rosarios today — slow and crowded, which is exactly the demand and the pain. There is no foiling incumbent; clean, low-wake operation suits the Corales del Rosario national park.

regulatory_note: Colombian jurisdiction: DIMAR (maritime authority) and the Sociedad Portuaria; the Corales del Rosario y San Bernardo national park imposes environmental rules that favor zero-emission, low-wake vessels.
seasonality: Cartagena sits at the southern edge of the Caribbean — largely below the main hurricane belt — supporting a long operating window; the dry season (Dec–Apr) is peak, with brisk December–March winds in the bay.
summary: Cartagena is Colombia's tourism jewel — a UNESCO walled city with a fast-growing luxury-hotel and events scene — and its weekend playground is the Rosario Islands and Barú, a national-park archipelago ~18 nm offshore. Today that transfer is a slow, often crowded launch from the city. A premium, quiet, faster service to the Rosarios and Barú is a clear tourism + luxury-charter opportunity, with the Cartagena bay itself supporting in-city water mobility.
tagline: A booming colonial-luxury city whose island playground is reached by a slow, crowded boat.
